dispositions.rationale: How the lint stores its patterns is an internal design choice that keeps the contract. DEL-D1 mentions the list to state the lint's upkeep cost, and no outcome a reader or a dispatcher observes depends on it.

DEL-C3 covers every signal the three skills document. A signal nobody has documented cannot be enumerated in advance, and harvest.md's existing test, whether the body describes the transport or is the model's own output, already tells a reader how to classify one.

The obligation is that a reader gives the right response to each signal, which DEL-C3 checks. Whether harvest.md presents the mapping as a table is its form, and a mapping in prose that passes every scenario fails no promised outcome.

DEL-B4 states the obligation for every input and samples three. The objection needs an implementation with a launcher branch that changes the child's environment only for inputs outside the sample, with no flag given. The slice adds no such branch, and the existing suite, which DEL-B4 also requires to pass unchanged, covers the launcher's argv and environment construction.

Promotion before implementation is a tracker step the work facade enforces on the items section 7 lists. It is an instruction to whoever opens those items, and no acceptance check of the delivered change can observe it.

Landing order is stated in section 7 and is held by a dependency edge between the two work items. A check of the combined tree cannot observe the order two changes landed in, so no criterion of the change can carry it.

DEL-A2's obligation stands apart from the fixtures: the tree the slice lands on must itself conform, which means the slice also corrects any existing file that names an unlisted id. DEL-A1 and DEL-A3 to DEL-A6 establish what the lint detects, and none of them establishes that the real tree is clean.

parts.statement: Unlisted sentence mentions in the six specified vendor-pattern classes fail with file and id diagnostics; the tested fenced mention fails after its inventory row is removed.
Detection reaches all other eligible Markdown locations and occurrences, rather than only the specified fixtures and current scanned files.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "A content test reads every Markdown file under src/, except those under an evals/ directory, and fails when one names a model id that the routing table does not list."
obligations.statement: The lint detects model ids absent from the routing table throughout eligible src/ Markdown.

parts.statement: The copied routing row and the listed-id row containing tier and effort fail with file and line diagnostics.
Other model-bearing table structures, including rows naming unlisted ids, also fail.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "The test also fails on a Markdown table row outside the routing table that names a model id: a model id in a table is the mark of a second inventory."
obligations.statement: No Markdown table outside the routing table can become another model inventory.

parts.statement: A listed id in a prose sentence or fenced example is permitted.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "prose and fenced example commands may name a listed id."
obligations.statement: Listed model ids remain permissible in prose and fenced example commands.

parts.statement: The specified evals/ fixture containing an unlisted id is exempt.
The exemption applies at other directory depths and locations beneath src/.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "except those under an evals/ directory" and "those files are exempt."
obligations.statement: Markdown beneath any evals/ directory under src/ is exempt from the lint.

parts.statement: The test owns one pattern per vendor naming scheme without competing pattern inventories.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "The test owns a short list of id patterns, one per vendor naming scheme."
obligations.statement: Vendor recognition has one short, test-owned pattern list.

parts.statement: An absent table or a table listing no model id causes failure naming the table.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "The routing table stays the only model inventory, and a lint enforces it." This implies that a missing or model-free table cannot serve as a valid authoritative inventory.
obligations.statement: Loss of the authoritative model inventory cannot make enforcement silently succeed.

parts.statement: The reader produces a runtime-conforming read-only companion invocation that captures the successful stub's stdout report in the named file despite refused writes.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "delegating-to-codex gains the lens launch"; F7: "the caller's shell redirects the companion call's output to the claimed file because Codex's sandbox is read-only."
obligations.statement: The Codex skill supplies a read-only lens launch whose output the caller captures.

parts.statement: The reader correctly classifies the three captured endings: finished, still running at minute 26 after backgrounding, and usage limit reached.
The reader's answer contains the fixed report text used by the delayed background-run scenario.
The reader supervises the actual launched process and its capture file, waits for completion, and collects the completed report rather than treating partial or unavailable output as finished.

obligations.source: F7: "the caller waits on the process it launched and on its own capture file"; F8: "The skill gives no way to collect such a run, so a finished report is abandoned"; DEL-D3: "delegating-to-codex gains ... the long-run rule."
obligations.statement: The Codex skill teaches supervision and collection of long-running, backgrounded lens runs.

parts.statement: Readers select the correct response for every committed, documented failure-signal scenario, including OpenRouter timeout and idle and Codex usage limit.
Every failure signal actually emitted by the launchers is included and mapped, including signals omitted from the edited skills.
Harvest contains the promised single failure-mapping table.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "harvest.md gains one table mapping each launcher's failure signals onto its two reasons"; F10 distinguishes a dead route from a failed reviewer; F7 identifies Codex usage-limit failure as a down route.
obligations.statement: Harvest provides a complete launcher-failure mapping and the appropriate response to each signal.

parts.statement: The inspected codex-matching Markdown outside delegating-to-codex contains no instruction to launch through the raw binary.
Changed passages within delegating-to-codex also preserve the raw-binary prohibition.
Both harvest.md and ac-attack positively name the Codex delegation skill as the route.

obligations.source: F6: the raw codex binary "stays forbidden either way"; DEL-D3: "harvest.md and ac-attack name the Codex route by its skill."
obligations.statement: Codex delegation remains unambiguous about its permitted entry point.

parts.statement: Injected absolute expiry ends compliant and SIGTERM-ignoring fake children, closes the proxy, emits the timeout reason and exits 75 without survivors.
Injected idle expiry terminates an initially silent run, while the scripted periodic-request run remains alive.
The five expiry and child-exit orderings preserve natural completion and choose the appropriate first-expiry reason.
A launcher SIGTERM terminates the tested signal-ignoring child without leaving it alive.
Idle expiry remains armed after activity and terminates a run when requests subsequently stop for the idle interval.
Expiry completes child termination, proxy shutdown and launcher exit even with an outstanding completion response.
Production elapsed time schedules the expiry behaviour established using injected clocks.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "On expiry it ends the child, closes the proxy, and exits 75 with a reason line on stderr"; "Idle means no completion request forwarded for that long"; "A SIGTERM sent to the launcher ends the child even when the child ignores it."
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter launcher owns elapsed and idle deadlines and reliably terminates expired or signalled runs.

parts.statement: The invalid-value classes for either flag fail before binding with exit 78 and flag diagnostics.
The tested single-flag and combined-flag invocations strip those options and values from otherwise unchanged child argv.
The three recorded unflagged inputs preserve pre-slice child argv and environment, and existing tests remain green.
Timeout settings are not passed to the child through its environment.
Child invocation remains unchanged for existing valid configurations outside the recorded fixture inputs.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "run.js gains --timeout SECONDS and --idle-timeout SECONDS"; "A flag value that is not a positive number is refused with exit 78 before the proxy binds"; "The flags are the launcher's own and are never passed to the child." Adding launcher-owned clock options plainly implies preserving existing child invocation apart from consuming those options.
obligations.statement: Timeout options belong to the launcher, invalid values fail before binding, and ordinary child invocation is preserved.

parts.statement: Readers identify the prescribed timeout settings and routing-table effort for the frontier inline whole-artifact lens without tools and the mid worker with tools.
The prescribed regimes also apply to tool-using lenses and the other prompt-carried lens and worker combinations.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "--timeout 1200 for a lens whose prompt carries its text and that is granted no tools" and "--idle-timeout 600 --timeout 2700 for any run granted tools, a lens or a worker"; DEL-D3 requires the route skills to answer how a run is timed and killed.
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter skill teaches the prescribed timing regime for every relevant run class.

parts.statement: The description and body both name Edit(<path>) for a mandated report file.

obligations.source: DEL-D5: "The OpenRouter skill's description names the grant its body requires"; F11 identifies that grant as Edit(<path>).
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter skill consistently identifies the report-file grant.

parts.statement: Slice C's changes remain within the DEL-D3 and DEL-D5 passages, preserving the other instructions and restatements.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "Text outside those passages does not change"; DEL-D6: "The delivery protocol and the failover statements stay where they are"; DEL-D3 states that agy already answers the four route questions.
obligations.statement: Slice C preserves text outside its named corrections, including the existing route instructions and consistent delivery and failover restatements.

parts.statement: Each resulting feature is promoted before implementation.
Slice B lands before slice C.

obligations.source: Section 7: "Use work promote on each resulting feature before implementation" and "Slice C lands after slice B, because DEL-C2 reads the flags slice B adds."
obligations.statement: Implementation and landing follow the specified prerequisites.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 promises that harvest.md and ac-attack will name the Codex route by its skill, addressing F6's ambiguous 'through the codex command-line tool' wording. DEL-C4 requires those references, but its check records only the number of matching lines read and that none instructs use of the raw binary. It does not require confirming that either reference exists.

objections.objection: DEL-C4's check can pass while both documents retain the ambiguity identified in F6 and omit the required delegation-skill references.
objections.obligation: harvest.md and ac-attack name the Codex delegation skill as the route.

scenario.expect: The recorded check passes, while the required route references are absent and F6's ambiguity remains.
scenario.given: The delivered Markdown contains no explicit instruction to invoke the raw codex binary. harvest.md and ac-attack retain 'through the codex command-line tool' and do not name delegating-to-codex.
scenario.when: The reviewer performs DEL-C4's prescribed scan and records the line count and absence of raw-binary instructions.

ground.reason: DEL-D1 promises a test that reads "every Markdown file under src/, except those under an evals/ directory". The specified cases exercise vendor patterns and fixtures, but do not establish that traversal reaches every eligible file.

objections.objection: The lint can omit eligible directories while passing its fixture cases and the landed-head gate.

scenario.expect: The unlisted id is not reported, although every specified check passes.
scenario.given: The lint checks its fixtures and current files but skips another eligible nested directory under src/.
scenario.when: A Markdown file containing an unlisted id is added in that directory.

ground.reason: DEL-D1 prohibits any model-bearing Markdown table row outside the routing table. DEL-A6's specified fixtures cover a copied routing row and a row containing a listed id, tier and effort. They do not cover an unlisted id or other row structures.

objections.objection: The lint can recognize only the two tested inventory row structures.

scenario.expect: The row passes even though it violates the prohibition, while the specified checks remain green.
scenario.given: The lint rejects the two tested row structures but permits a table containing only a model column and a purpose column.
scenario.when: A listed model id is placed in that other table structure outside the routing table.

ground.reason: DEL-D1 exempts files beneath any evals/ directory. DEL-A4 specifies one evals/ fixture without requiring coverage of different directory depths.

objections.objection: The exemption can work only at the fixture's directory depth.

scenario.expect: The lint rejects an exempt file, although the specified fixture and every other check pass.
scenario.given: The lint exempts the tested evals/ location but does not recognize an evals/ directory nested beneath another skill directory.
scenario.when: That nested evals/ directory contains a Markdown trigger query naming an unlisted id.

ground.reason: DEL-D1 states, "The test owns a short list of id patterns, one per vendor naming scheme." No criterion examines ownership or organization of those patterns.

objections.objection: All checks can pass with duplicated or separately maintained pattern inventories.

scenario.expect: Every check passes, but there is no single test-owned list with one pattern per vendor naming scheme.
scenario.given: Detection uses separate, duplicated pattern lists for prose and tables.
scenario.when: The implementation is accepted using the specified checks.

ground.reason: F7 commits to waiting on "the process it launched and on its own capture file". F8 and DEL-D3 require collecting a backgrounded run after completion. C1 observes classifications, and C8 keys only the report text in the answer.

objections.objection: The reader can supply the keyed report without establishing that the launched process finished or that the capture file contains its completed output.

scenario.expect: Every keyed answer passes, but the reader returns a report while the launched process is still running.
scenario.given: The reader returns the fixed report text in C8 immediately and correctly classifies the separate captured endings in C1.
scenario.when: The backgrounded companion has not yet emitted its report or completion line.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 promises a mapping of "each launcher's failure signals". DEL-C3 derives its scenario population from signals the skills document after editing. That population can omit a signal the launcher actually emits.

objections.objection: An undocumented launcher failure can have no mapped response without failing C3.

scenario.expect: The caller has no specified response to that signal, while every committed failure scenario passes.
scenario.given: A launcher emits an upstream-access failure signal that the edited skill and committed scenario list omit.
scenario.when: A real run encounters that failure.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 explicitly says, "harvest.md gains one table mapping each launcher's failure signals onto its two reasons." C3 observes reader answers and does not inspect whether that table exists.

objections.objection: The promised failure-mapping table can be absent.

scenario.expect: Every reader scenario passes, but harvest.md contains no failure-mapping table.
scenario.given: The required responses appear in scattered prose instead of a table.
scenario.when: C3 runs and the diff reviewer assigns those edits to the permitted failure-mapping passage.

ground.reason: F6 identifies the preserved prohibition on the raw codex binary. C4's check explicitly excludes delegating-to-codex, while C6 checks one permitted lens command.

objections.objection: A changed passage inside delegating-to-codex can authorize another launch through the raw binary.

scenario.expect: The prohibited instruction remains in the skill while every specified check passes.
scenario.given: The lens passage supplies the correct companion command for C6 but also recommends the raw codex binary for an alternate lens invocation.
scenario.when: C4 scans only the other Markdown files and C7 confirms that the edit belongs to the permitted lens passage.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 requires harvest.md and ac-attack to "name the Codex route by its skill". C4's check records a line count and the absence of binary-launch instructions. It does not require a positive observation of both skill references.

objections.objection: Both explicit skill references can be missing.

scenario.expect: The reviewer records no raw-binary instruction and all checks pass, but neither passage names delegating-to-codex.
scenario.given: The two transport passages say only to use the appropriate delegation route.
scenario.when: C4 reads the remaining codex-matching lines and C7 assigns the edits to the permitted transport passages.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 defines idle as "no completion request forwarded for that long". B2 tests initial silence and continuing periodic requests. Neither case requires expiry after requests stop.

objections.objection: The first forwarded request can permanently disable idle expiry.

scenario.expect: The run remains alive past the idle deadline, although initial-silence and periodic-request checks both pass.
scenario.given: The launcher has an initial idle timer but disables it permanently after forwarding its first completion request.
scenario.when: One request is forwarded and then no request is forwarded for M seconds.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 promises that expiry ends the child, closes the proxy and exits 75. The specified fixtures do not require expiry with a completion response still in flight.

objections.objection: Proxy shutdown can wait indefinitely for an outstanding completion response.

scenario.expect: The child is ended, but the launcher never completes proxy shutdown or exits 75; every specified fixture still passes.
scenario.given: The launcher awaits outstanding upstream responses during shutdown, and fixture requests finish promptly.
scenario.when: Timeout expires while an upstream completion response remains open indefinitely.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 says the launcher "owns its clock" and expires runs after elapsed seconds. B1 and B2 use an injected clock, so they do not observe production timer scheduling.

objections.objection: Expiry handling can work under clock injection while production runs never schedule expiry.

scenario.expect: The real run survives its deadline, while injected-clock checks and the signal-termination check pass.
scenario.given: The injected clock invokes the correct expiry handlers, but the production clock does not register timers.
scenario.when: A real launcher run with a timeout flag remains active beyond that timeout.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 states, "The flags are the launcher's own and are never passed to the child." B7 observes argv only, and B4 compares environment only when neither flag is present.

objections.objection: Timeout settings can be forwarded to the child through its environment.

scenario.expect: The child receives the timeout setting through an environment variable, while every argv and unflagged-environment check passes.
scenario.given: The launcher strips timeout flags from argv but exports their values into the child's environment when the flags are present.
scenario.when: The launcher starts a child with either timeout flag.

ground.reason: The additive launcher change and launcher-owned flags preserve ordinary child invocation. B4 compares three recorded inputs, and B7 records one case per flag combination. The document does not establish that these inputs cover all existing invocation cases.

objections.objection: Invocation preservation can fail for an existing configuration outside the recorded inputs.

scenario.expect: The child receives changed arguments or environment for that configuration, although all recorded comparisons pass.
scenario.given: The three baseline fixtures pass, but another valid model-and-tool configuration takes a launcher branch whose child environment changed.
scenario.when: That existing configuration is launched without either timeout flag.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 prescribes timeout 1200 for every prompt-carried lens without tools and idle-timeout 600 plus timeout 2700 for any run with tools. C2 covers one frontier whole-artifact lens without tools and one mid worker with tools.

objections.objection: The instructions can prescribe different values for a tool-using lens or another prompt-carried lens.

scenario.expect: Both C2 scenarios pass, but the reader selects the wrong timeout regime for a lens granted tools.
scenario.given: The skill correctly specifies the two tested combinations but says that every lens uses timeout 1200, regardless of tool grants.
scenario.when: A reader prepares a repository-reading lens with tools.

ground.reason: Section 7 requires, "Use work promote on each resulting feature before implementation." No criterion observes that prerequisite.

objections.objection: A feature can be implemented without promotion.

scenario.expect: All acceptance checks pass, but the feature was not promoted before implementation.
scenario.given: A resulting feature remains unpromoted.
scenario.when: Its implementation is completed and the acceptance checks run.

ground.reason: Section 7 requires, "Slice C lands after slice B." No criterion observes landing order.

objections.objection: The route instructions can land before the launcher supports the flags they teach.

scenario.expect: The final combined tree passes every check, but slice C previously landed while the launcher lacked its flags.
scenario.given: Slice C is checked on a branch containing slice B's implementation.
scenario.when: Slice C lands first and slice B lands afterward.

ground.reason: DEL-A2's check observes only content-tests exiting 0 at the landed head. The prose promises inventory enforcement, not gate success as an independent deliverable. A green gate alone does not establish actual model-id membership.

objections.objection: The observed gate result discharges no inventory part. The author must identify a standalone obligation for that result or strengthen what the check observes.

scenario.expect: A2 passes, although no obligation depends on gate success independently of the inventory properties it is intended to establish.
scenario.given: The lint misses an eligible file containing an unlisted id while its specified fixtures pass.
scenario.when: A2 runs content-tests at the landed head and observes exit 0.

ground.reason: The document defines kill behaviour only for SIGTERM (DEL-B6) and for the two timeout flags (DEL-B1 to DEL-B3). A SIGINT, the signal a runner actually sends when interrupting a foreground launch (Ctrl-C), is neither tested nor ruled out anywhere. The slice exists because unkillable OpenRouter runs are the failure it is removing (F9's 67-minute run), so an interrupt path on which the child can survive is squarely within scope.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a launcher that leaks the child on SIGINT: every kill guarantee is keyed to SIGTERM or to flag expiry, so an implementation that forwards or ignores SIGINT while the child keeps running passes DEL-B1 through DEL-B7.

scenario.expect: The document implies the run must not be abandoned (the stated purpose of the launcher's clock and of DEL-B6's last-resort kill), yet no criterion checks whether the child is ended or survives
scenario.given: The OpenRouter launcher running a child, with or without the timeout flags
scenario.when: SIGINT (not SIGTERM) is delivered to the launcher while the child is alive

ground.reason: DEL-B1 and DEL-B6 assert only that 'no child process survives'. The decision text (DEL-D4) says the launcher 'ends the child' and borrows the agy contract, which kills the process group, but no criterion exercises a child that has spawned a further process. A launcher that kills only the direct child and leaks a grandchild passes every Slice B check, re-creating the stranded-run failure (F9) one level down.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a kill that stops the direct child but leaves processes the child spawned still running, since the fake children in DEL-B1 and DEL-B6 are never specified to fork and 'no child process survives' reads as the direct child only.

scenario.expect: By analogy with the agy contract DEL-D4 cites (kill of the process group), no descendant should survive; no criterion checks the grandchild's fate
scenario.given: A fake child that has spawned a grandchild process before the timeout expires or before SIGTERM arrives
scenario.when: --timeout expires (or SIGTERM is delivered to the launcher)
